chapter: Maynard Ferguson and Dizzy's big band
title: Maynard Ferguson's air and consistency
summary: Ferguson never missed notes and had huge lung capacity.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What kind of physical toll does that take?

You have to be in good physical shape to even think about doing what he was doing, but it wasn’t a thing that you in most cases could develop on your own. He got – when he took – when he inhaled, he got a lot more air than most people do. He got about twice the amount of air that most humans get when he inhales.
Is that because of, I want to say, his structural capacity as a person? Or something he trained himself to do?

I think it was his natural structural capacity. He had a larger lung than most people. The amount of air that he got in was just impossible. That’s part of the reason he was able to keep the notes up.
And be true, in the center of the note, at . . .
Yeah, because if you don’t have air, you wouldn’t be able to be real consistent. You could play high, but you couldn’t be real consistent. But he was very consistent.
